data.title: Podvrščie – a Slavic barrow cemetery at Sverepec
data.excerpt: The small Slavic barrow cemetery of Podvrščie in the cadastral area of Sverepec holds the burials of warriors from the 9th and 10th centuries. In November 2015 our Hradiská civic association cleared the impenetrably overgrown site and opened it up to the public, together with an unusual pit and boulder that strongly evoke a sacrificial site.

children.text: On Saturday 7 November 2015 our Hradiská civic association, together with enthusiasts from Sverepec (Ján Hôrkový, Mgr. Juraj Kalo and Michal Richtárik), cleared the small Slavic barrow cemetery of Podvrščie, which lies in the cadastral area of the village of Sverepec. Slavic warriors of the 9th and 10th centuries were buried in the barrows. Barrow burial was practised in pre-Christian times.

The whole barrow cemetery was overgrown with a literally impenetrable jungle of thorns and dog-rose scrub, which made it practically inaccessible. The result of our day-long work is a cleared barrow cemetery together with the unusual pit and boulder already described by A. Petrovský-Šichman, which strongly evoke a sacrificial site. The barrow cemetery, which lies a few minutes’ walk from the village, has thus been opened up to the public, and at the beginning of next year we plan to place an information panel there in cooperation with the village of Sverepec. It will be the first Slavic barrow cemetery in Slovakia to be marked and opened up in this way. Thanks go to everyone from our association who took part in the event, as well as to the lads from Sverepec, who helped us a great deal. We also thank the owner of the land, Mrs Eva Martišíková from Sverepec, for giving her consent to the clearance.
